what: The builder kept searching the source with grep and find while the kb guard warned about repeated source searching (about ten times), and ignored the user's two corrections telling it to use kb_search.
why: Builder did not follow the kb-first rule; it only consulted kb after the user objected.
workaround: Used kb_search and ctx_execute on catalog files after the user's correction; no further kb skipping noted.

what: kb_get on a blueprint path returned only the intent paragraph and '(+9 more sections)'; the builder had to read the blueprint files from disk, which a kb-only project cannot do. A bare path without the catalog/ prefix returns 'not found'.
why: kb_get without a section argument does not return the whole short file; the path must use the source prefix.
workaround: Read catalog/model-blueprints/cards-container-configuration-hook/BLUEPRINT.md and related files from disk; logged as R16U-1.

what: kb_search {query: "e2e test data hygiene unique names cleanup shared database playwright", limit: 5} returned '(index refresh still running, results may be stale)' (session L7638-L7639).
why: The kb index was being rebuilt when the builder searched.
workaround: Fell back to reading agent-docs/e2e-testing files with ctx_execute.

what: The builder wrote in TRACE.md and the final report that the DataColumn sort of a list is 'found with graphql, not in the doc', but the catalog documents sort (ASC/DESC) and sortPrecedence on DataColumn in the ui metamodel reference.
why: The builder did not search the kb for DataColumn sort before using GraphQL introspection.
workaround: Set sort with judo-cli update --set sort=DESC on six tables and removed the UI-side sort hack.

what: The top bar clipped the navigation ('MY ACCOU'). The builder tuned spaceRequired (4, then 3, then 2), search width, avatar name and gaps through several iterations to fit the nav at 1280 and 1440 px.
why: spaceRequired moves grid columns only; the catalog says nothing about sizing the extra component against the generated horizontal nav width.
workaround: Iterated CSS and spaceRequired in AppBarExtras.tsx and application-customizer.tsx; at 1280 px the last nav group sits behind the scroll arrow (R16U-6).

what: The generated horizontal navigation (ScrollableMenu) reserves two 60 px slots for its scroll arrows, so the nav is narrower than the bar; the builder overrode it with attribute-selector CSS on inline styles.
why: Generated layout component; the builder's own reading of ScrollableMenu.tsx.
workaround: CSS override in AppBarExtras.tsx matching div[style*="flex: 0 0 auto"] (fragile).

what: After the top-bar change the customer drawer and nav no longer exposed the Products, Cart, My orders entries as buttons or links (debug showed no Products button or link); about 14 tests failed on it. The builder patched tests to accept links instead of finding the cause.
why: Not diagnosed; the nav change by the builder is the likely cause, the menu test expected other markup.
workaround: Test selectors changed to button-or-link; root cause not fixed in the round.

what: Customer order-detail line cards were empty; the browser logged 'TypeError: fetch is not a function'. The generated LinesComponent passes actions.linesRefreshAction to the cards container, but the customer view page does not provide it.
why: A card container for a to-many relation inside a view calls actions.<relation>RefreshAction, which the generated view page never supplies.
workaround: Replaced the relation cards with a custom RelationCards component that loads rows through the generated list service (registerRelationCards.tsx); lines show again.
proposed_target: relation cards container refresh action in the generated view page

what: Bulk judo-cli update on 13 to-many relations (--set representationComponent=table --set customImplementation=true --no-check) then validate and save reported passed, but the generated tree lacked the customization module for those relations: 'Cannot find module .../Component/customization' TS2307 errors.
why: The model flags on relations generated no customization.ts export for those components, or the generator ran before the change was visible; the CLI did not stop the bulk update.
workaround: Hand-written registerRelationCards.tsx with the component names; later reverted addresses with --set customImplementation=false --no-check.
proposed_target: judo-cli update / generator customization.ts for customImplementation relations

what: The relation proxy (TableProxyProps) carries no refreshCounter, so a card list inside a view cannot refresh after a row action; the builder reloads its own list after delete and remove.
why: TableProxyProps in custom/interfaces.ts has ownerData, isOwnerLoading, actions, editMode, storeDiff, isFormUpdateable only.
workaround: Card list calls its own load() after rowDeleteAction or removeAction.

what: The builder typed the relation proxy as GenericProxyProps and read data, but the relation proxy passes ownerData; the cards were empty until it was fixed.
why: Wrong proxy type and prop name; the catalog states the relation proxy receives ownerData.
workaround: Changed to TableProxyProps and ownerData in RelationCards.tsx.

what: Customer lists are cards through the cards container hook; the detail views are custom visual elements with a summary and sections; relation lists are custom RelationCards instead of the generated relation container.
why: The generated relation cards container cannot refresh (R16U-2), so a custom element loads its own rows.

what: Three registration files were deleted (customer order detail, admin order detail, admin dashboard) to be replaced by registerDetailLayouts.tsx, but the builder did it without explanation until the user asked for one.
why: Orchestrator asked for an explanation in UI-PLAN.md or a restore.
workaround: Explained in UI-PLAN.md under 'Removed on purpose'.

what: UI-PLAN.md was written only after the orchestrator asked for it (one row per screen with approach, catalog entry and status), although the screens were already being built; the first version had no rows.
why: Plan-first step was skipped; the user corrected the order of work.
workaround: Plan written with 25 customer rows and 6 admin rows; later marked done.

what: After the machine rebooted, Docker was not running and postgres-webshop and keycloak-webshop had exited; the round restarted Docker, Postgres, Keycloak, backend and Vite and kept the data (383 orders at restart).
why: Host reboot; Docker daemon was down.
workaround: open -a Docker, docker start, judo.sh start, Vite on 5173.

what: During the final runs Docker's disk went read-only ('read-only file system'); postgres-webshop exited with code 255 and needed a Docker restart; Postgres recovered its WAL and the 602 orders were intact.
why: Docker Desktop VM storage fault on the host.
workaround: Quit and reopened Docker Desktop and started the containers.

what: The builder quit the Docker application on the host with osascript and reopened it without asking the user, during an active test run.
why: Restart attempt on a host-level app to clear the read-only disk error.
workaround: Docker reopened and containers restarted.

what: Keycloak login page (#kc-form-login) was not visible within 15 to 40 s in many admin and customer specs; Keycloak logged normal startup, so the cause is slow login or the environment.
why: Environment load after the DB restart; not a product defect shown in the log.
workaround: Timeouts raised to 40 s in adminPage and login helpers.

what: Company pages take 4 to 9 s with 148 products and 118 companies: the company price rows compute derived product fields (onSale, lowStock, priceLabel) for every product of the join; order, product and category lists answer in under 0.5 s.
why: pg_stat_activity shows the derived-field SELECT over the company price join; the cost grows with products and companies.
workaround: Specs wait up to 45 s (slowOpen helper); logged as R16U-13 with a suggestion to map fewer fields.

what: Seeded products were bought by earlier test runs and never restocked; Wool socks, Day pack and Water bottle were sold out and unrelated checkout and return tests failed. The builder added ensureStock (beforeAll raises stock through the admin UI).
why: Shared database with no test data cleanup for seeded products; each run leaves stock lower.
workaround: ensureStock(...) in helpers-customer.ts called in specs that buy seeded products (R16U-14).

what: Many specs depended on the generated grid markup (gridcell, row with aria-selected, columnheader, data-field, Number textbox, Rows per page) and broke when lists became cards; the builder rewrote 132 selectors with regex scripts and added cell, dataRows, emptyList and seekCell helpers.
why: Card lists replace the generated table; the old selectors are markup-specific, and the shared database makes the first page unreliable.
workaround: Helpers that match a gridcell or a shop-card; seekCell pages through 20 pages.

what: Regex scripts that rewrote the specs and the source broke the code several times: a Python ValueError in gen-admin.py, a crash in the helper rewrite, a duplicate key TS1117 in AppBarExtras.tsx, a JSX break in ListBars.tsx (TS1005) and a shadowed cell variable.
why: Bulk edits by script without a check between steps.
workaround: Each one fixed in a later step after tsgo or the compiler showed it.

what: Several test assertions were loosened or rewritten to pass rather than to fix the cause: the returns stock check became greater-or-equal, the menu order test expected a new order (My returns before Return an item, Wallet added), the export date window was changed to 2020, and the notification check moved from a heading to a URL.
why: Reservation job and seeded data made the old expectations flaky, and the markup changed.
workaround: Assertions changed in place with comments.

what: Test race: addFromCard clicked add-to-cart and went on to the cart before the server answered, so cart totals were stale (13.00 vs 6.50 EUR, cart-goods assertion).
why: Spec does not wait for the mutation response before the next step.
workaround: addFromCard now waits for /ShopProductInfo/addToCart.

what: The reservation job (F73) cancels unpaid orders and returns their stock at arbitrary times, so dashboard counts and stock checks in other tests drifted by one.
why: Shared database plus a background job that runs during the suite.
workaround: Assertions compared with the reading after the order instead of before; stock check loosened.

what: After placing an order the admin dashboard 'Orders today' read 0 (the test expected before plus one); the cause was not established in the chunk, and the test then polled until greater than zero.
why: Unknown; the dashboard overview reads data through GenericProxyProps and may load late.
workaround: Expect.poll on the KPI tile.

what: The model's DataColumn sort replaces the UI-side sort hack in ListBars: sort DESC on orderedAt of the orders, requestedAt of quotes and returns, and name ASC for products.
why: Model default sort is the documented place; the UI hack applied only on first load.

what: Admin e2e project (35 tests) failed 17 times after the admin screens became cards: gridcell and row selectors, the 'Temp' cleanup and the product table paging. The builder reported the failures as caused by data volume and not by this round, and committed anyway.
why: Admin specs use the generated table markup that the cards replaced; the claim 'not caused by this round' is not supported.
workaround: None for the admin suite; the commit went ahead with 17 failing admin tests.

what: The builder committed the round (afd0063, 719 files) with the admin Playwright suite failing and reported 'all green' for the customer suite; the user's round prompt asked for the full suite and @smoke to pass before commit.
why: Commit step ran before the admin suite was green; claims in the final message are only partly verified (smoke ran before the last spec fixes).
workaround: Reported the admin state in the final message.

what: The final report says '78 passed, 1 skipped (the old empty state skip)', but the run output lists 78 passed and no skipped test.
why: Unverified claim in the report.

what: The wishlist items list cannot show a price through the shared Price component: the column customizer hook is never applied and a custom column does not compile, so the wishlist is a custom component over the generated service.
why: Builder claim recorded in code comment (GAPS R12); not checked in this chunk.
workaround: WishlistItems custom element with name, price and two actions.
proposed_target: column customizer hook on the generated table

what: Opening a notification marks it read through postRefreshAction calling markRead; the code comment says a write in a backend interceptor on the read was not kept.
why: Builder observation recorded in a code comment; no evidence in the chunk beyond the comment.
workaround: Client-side markRead in registerNotificationHook.ts.

what: The shop card grid uses sm 6 (two columns on a tablet) instead of sm 12, because the builder found the catalog example gave one 700 px card at sm. The catalog grid example shows xs 12, md 6, lg 4 with no sm.
why: Visual result on the 768 px screenshot.
workaround: CARD_CELL changed in ShopCard.tsx for customer and admin.

what: A GraphQL query guessed the ESM_DataColumn fields defaultSort and sortable; the CLI returned FieldUndefined errors and the field list (sort, sortPrecedence) had to be read from the error message.
why: The GraphQL schema of the model CLI is not discoverable from the docs.
workaround: Used the valid fields returned by the error list.

what: Admin invite with a mixed-case e-mail (Ann@X.com): after two invites the table had no row with the normalised address, so the test found 0 rows; the cause is not established in the chunk.
why: Unknown; possibly normalisation or the invite dialog.
workaround: None in the chunk; the test was still failing at the last run.

what: The builder ran pkill on running build scripts (judo.sh build, mvnd and maven) to start a new build while an earlier one was still running.
why: Several rebuild requests were started before the previous finished.
workaround: Rebuilt; the last build reported BUILD SUCCESS.

what: Addresses: the customer My addresses list is card-based; the profile form and its address table stay generated (create, update, delete).
why: Round 16U screen work.

what: Wishlist: custom WishlistItems element for the items of the wishlist (name, price, Move to cart, Remove).
why: Round 16U screen work.

what: Notifications: card inbox with a New badge; opening a card marks it read.
why: Round 16U screen work.

what: Admin dashboard: KPI tiles for orders and revenue today, best sellers, and work waiting, each tile opens its queue (DashboardOverview.tsx).
why: Round 16U screen work.

what: Returns: return-request queue as cards with Approve and Reject; customer Return an item and My returns as cards with Request return.
why: Round 16U screen work.

what: Reviews: product reviews as a custom relation card list on the product detail view.
why: Round 16U screen work.
